Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title="ARC task-c10e4434: compress crossing stripe grid", id="arc_task_c10e4434_compress_crossing_stripe_grid", path="arc-patterns", global_=True, content="For ARC task-c10e4434, the input is a rectangular grid with some full-width horizontal colored stripe rows and full-height vertical colored stripe columns; all other cells are largely background. Compress each region between successive stripe lines to one representative row/column, retaining every stripe line as its own row/column. The output therefore alternates representative gap rows/columns with the colored stripe rows/columns: output height = 2*(number of horizontal stripes)+1, width = 2*(number of vertical stripes)+1. Use any one representative from each gap since cells within a gap band are equivalent for this pattern. Preserve all values at intersections exactly as shown, including cases where a horizontal stripe overrides a vertical stripe at one crossing. Example observed: 10x11 input with horizontal stripe rows 1 (color 3), 6 (color 5), vertical stripe cols 3 (color 8), 8 (color 6) compresses to a 5x5 grid alternating the four gap regions and the two stripe positions in each axis; chosen source rows [0,1,2,6,9], cols [0,3,5,8,10]. On test 12x13, stripes at rows 3,6,9 and cols 2,5,7,10 yielded 7x9 output; keep anomalous intersection r9,c5=8 as supplied." )
